faq.question: Is Scheduling Wizard compliant with ACGME rules for emergency medicine?

faq.answer: Most emergency medicine scheduling software is self-service, meaning a chief resident must learn the platform, enter all the rules, and troubleshoot conflicts themselves. Scheduling Wizard is a managed service. Programs submit their rules and receive finished, ACGME-compliant schedules as ready-to-use Excel files. There is no software to learn and no platform to operate.
faq.question: How is Scheduling Wizard different from other emergency medicine scheduling software?

faq.answer: Scheduling Wizard generates block and rotation schedules, call schedules, clinic schedules, and attending schedules for emergency medicine programs. All schedule types are optimized simultaneously so that a change in one does not create conflicts in another. Finished schedules are delivered as Excel spreadsheets.
faq.question: What types of EM schedules does Scheduling Wizard generate?

faq.answer: Yes. Many Scheduling Wizard clients use the platform they already have for day-to-day schedule viewing. Scheduling Wizard handles the schedule creation and optimization, and the finished Excel file can be uploaded directly into whatever platform you already use. The two tools serve different functions and work well alongside each other.
faq.question: Can Scheduling Wizard integrate with your existing platform?

faq.answer: When an unexpected absence occurs, Scheduling Wizard rapidly re-optimizes the affected portion of the schedule to restore coverage. This avoids the manual process of reshuffling assignments and checking every downstream impact by hand. ACGME compliance is maintained throughout the re-optimization.
faq.question: What happens when an EM resident has an unplanned absence?

faq.answer: Chief resident transitions are one of the most common sources of scheduling disruption in EM programs. With Scheduling Wizard, your program's rule configurations and scheduling rules persist with the service year over year. Incoming chief residents inherit a fully working, optimized scheduling system instead of starting from scratch with a blank spreadsheet.
